章节.Incorporating the MoHaYuni 61 into the M: The only surviving car, 61001, was incorporated into the MoHaYuni 44 type, also a third-class baggage-and-mail combined car, and renumbered 44100. At this time the pantograph was relocated to the front. Around the same time it was transferred to the Kitamatsumoto Depot and came to be operated on the Oito Line.
章节.Renewal Repair II and other modification:
In the 1950s, as the postwar confusion settled down somewhat, the measures taken to prevent train fires after the Sakuragicho accident were incorporated, and Renewal Repair (Renewal Repair II) came to be carried out again. The content differed depending on the works and the time, but the main work content is listed below.
Replacement of ventilators (Garland-type ventilator → globe-type ventilator)
To strengthen insulation, the raised steel-plate roof was made an ordinary wooden roof, and the rain-gutter position was unified to a lower position
Replacement of passenger doors with steel-plate pressed doors
Replacement of the wooden interior parts
Enlargement of the front run-number window (2 digits → 3 digits)
Filling in of the destination-display windows on the side fascia
Through this renewal repair, the variety of the original form, such as raised roofs and the number of ventilators, was almost lost, and the appearance became uniform. Not all of these work menu items were carried out on all cars; in the early period there were cars that kept their raised roofs while having globe-type ventilators fitted, and cars that remained with Garland-type ventilators. Also, because detailed specifications were changed according to the time of work, the variety of details became even richer.
In addition, the strengthened-illumination 250W headlight adopted to counter collision accidents with falling rocks on the Iida Line, having given good results, spread to all line sections using EMUs and was fitted to this series as well. At this time, the bullet-shaped and flush-mounted ones became the normal type, but some remained flush-mounted.
Other modifications are as follows.
章节.Three-door conversion of 51073 (renewal: 51073, which was transferred to the Hanwa Line in 1950, was used for a while after its transfer in the very form of the MoHa 42 type. In the 1953 renewal repair it was made 3-door semi-cross seating, and the traces of the rear cab were smoothed out and a 550 mm-wide window was provided in the crew-door portion. As a result, the window arrangement also became d1D25D42D11. At the same time, the motor was also replaced with the MT30, the same as the MoHa 54 type, to strengthen the output. Before the renewal repair, 51073 was an odd car—a 2-door MoHa 51—but after the renewal repair, although it became 3-door, its motor output improved to the level of the MoHa 54 type, so in a different way from before it became an odd car among the MoHa 51 type.
章节.Gear-ratio change of the MoHa 54 100-num: Among the MoHa 54 type, the 100-number series incorporated from the MoHa 60 type, though made semi-cross seating, kept the gear ratio of the MoHa 60 type at 1:2.87. Since this would overload the main motor during high-speed operation, it was changed to 1:2.56, the same as the MoHa 54 prototype cars, at the time of the 1954 renewal repair, aligning it with the MoHa 51 and MoHa 70 types, which likewise had high-speed gear ratios.
章节.Converting the KuHa 55 (KuroHa 59 conver:
The KuroHa 59 converted from the former SaRoHa 46, because its second-class compartment portion was wider than the KuroHa 59 prototype cars, was incorporated into express formations as noted above, so its downgrading conversion to KuHa 55 was late, in 1943. Of these, except for 59022, which was converted to four doors (via 55106, renumbered 85026 → 79056), 59023 - 59025 were converted to 55107 - 55109 without going through conversion to the KuHa 68 type. This group, together with the group converted directly from the KuroHa 59 type to the KuHa 55 type (55110 - 55114, of which 55114 was written off due to war damage), was excluded from the semi-cross-seating modification of the KuHa 55 type belonging to the Keihanshin local line, but to reinforce the semi-cross-seat cars of the Keihanshin local line, they underwent the semi-cross-seating modification from 1954 to 1955 and were incorporated into the KuHa 68 type. The renumbering is as follows.
68107[II] ← 55107 ← 59023 ← 46015 ← 46101
68109[II] ← 55108 ← 59024 ← 46016 ← 46102
68111 ← 55109 ← 59025 ← 46017 ← 46103
Whereas the window arrangement of 68001 - 68023 converted from the former KuroHa 59 is d1D25D311D2, this group's is d1D231D42D2, which differs; also, the cab, while the former is a half-compartment cab, is a full-compartment cab here.
章节.Converting 51078 to the Moya 4700 type: In 1958, 51078 was converted at the Toyokawa Branch Works into the overhead-wire test car Moya 4700. Because the body and bogies were newly built, only some of the electrical equipment used parts from the donor car. The following year, under the revision of the vehicle designation regulations, it was renumbered KuMoya 93000, and became famous for achieving, in 1960, the then-world record for narrow-gauge maximum speed of 175 km/h. Note that the donor car 51078 was a conversion from 41010, but there is a theory that, due to the wartime confusion, the actual car was swapped for 40001, the first-numbered MoHa 40.
章节.The 1959 revision of the vehicle designa:
Under this revision, motor cars with a cab became control motor cars (symbol: Kumo), so the MoHa 51 type was renamed KuMoHa 51 and the MoHa 54 type KuMoHa 54. Also, whereas previously types were expressed by numbers alone, from this revision the type symbol and the number were combined to form the type (e.g., type 69 → type KuroHa 69).
Also, from this period, modifications were carried out to cope with the intensifying commuter transport.
章节.Downgrading conversion of the KuroHa 69:
The KuroHa 69 type, which after the second-class restoration had been active as the star of the Keihanshin local line, saw its raison d'etre decline after the coupling of SaRo 85 cars to rapid services began in 1961. In October 1962 the coupling of KuroHa cars on the Keihanshin local line was abolished on the grounds of easing congestion, so over the following year the partitions of the first-class and second-class compartments (changed to a two-class system from 1960) were removed, longitudinal seating was adopted, and a downgrading conversion to the KuHa 55 type (KuHa 55151 - 55171 (odd numbers only)) was carried out. The work was done at the Suita Works for 55104(55151) and at the Hatsukaichi Works for the rest. The old-new number comparison is as follows.

章节.Door-addition modification of the Yokosu:
From 1963 to 1964, for the 2-door KuMoHa 43 and KuMoHa 53 (42 series), KuHa 47 (32 series), and SaHa 48 (52 series) remaining on the Yokosuka Line, in order to cope with the intensified commuter transport, to align the boarding positions when coupled with the 3-door 70 series, and to avoid disturbing orderly queuing, work was carried out at the Ofuna Works to add a passenger door in the center of the body and convert them to three doors. After the modification, the KuMoHa 43 type was changed to the KuMoHa 51 type (200-number series) and the KuHa 47 type to the KuHa 68 type (200-number series, 210-number series), while the KuMoHa 53 type and SaHa 48 type were given the new types KuMoHa 50 and SaHa 58 respectively. Of these, only KuHa 47002 was a car used on the Iida Line, but both the time of modification and the time of transfer out to the Niigata area were almost the same as for the other cars belonging to the Yokosuka Line. The renumbering situation is as follows.
Of these, the KuHa 68 200-number series are conversions from the KuHa 47 prototype cars, and the KuHa 68 210-number series are conversions from SaHa 48-converted cars. The reason the SaHa 58 has finely divided number series relative to its count is that the donor cars each differ (0-number series ← SaHa 48 of the narrow-window Ryuden formation, 10-number series ← SaHa 48 of the semi-streamlined 43 series formation, 20-number series ← SaHa 48 of the wide-window Ryuden formation, 50-number series ← SaHa 48 converted from the former SaRoHa 66 of the wide-window Ryuden formation); SaHa 58050 appeared at the time of renewal repair retaining its raised roof (in later years its rain gutters were modified to the same height as the other cars, but whereas the others were wooden, these were steel). Also, with the appearance of the KuMoHa 50 type, it would not have been strange to incorporate the KuMoHa 51073, a 42-series-converted output-strengthened car, into the KuMoHa 50, and there apparently was a plan to renumber it KuMoHa 50051, but in the end, without renumbering, it was converted to KuMoHa 51830. The side window arrangement of this group is made front-rear asymmetric with an independent door-pocket window supported by H rubber behind the door newly provided in the center, differing from KuMoHa 51073 (for example, the KuMoHa 50 type and KuMoHa 51 200-number series are d1D24D142D2).
Note that KuMoHa 50006 was involved in the Tsurumi accident that occurred on November 9, 1963 immediately after leaving the works; the body was wrecked beyond recognition and the car was written off.
章节.Increase in renewal-repair specification: From around this time, examples came to be seen of extensive use of H rubber on the cab windows and door-pocket windows to prevent corrosion from rainwater ingress; among these, in cars worked at the Suita Works, when the cab windows were H-rubbered, a hemispherical ventilator was fitted beside the gangway door, and together with the H-rubbered and miniaturized cab windows this formed a distinctive front. Also, of the cars fitted with hemispherical ventilators, many filled in the louvers above the cab windows, but some cars remained as they were.
章节.Transfer to the provinces (1960 - ):
The 51 series, which had been used as the mainstay of the Keihanshin local line, from the 1960s gradually came to be transferred to provincial lines, with the transfer of 72 series to the Keihanshin local line and the new-build assignment of 103 series accompanying the strengthening of transport capacity and the opening of newly electrified sections. Also, cars assigned to the Yokosuka Line and Hanwa Line were transferred to provincial lines as each line section's cars were replaced. Upon transfer to provincial lines, modifications such as lowering the roof and installing toilets according to the circumstances of the line section were carried out; in addition, to cope with gradients and short inter-station distances, mainly on cars assigned to the Shizuoka Railway Administration Bureau, the gears were changed to the same low-speed type as the 40 series.
The lines to which they were redeployed were mostly lines acquired from private railways during the war—the Senseki Line within the jurisdiction of the Sendai Railway Administration Bureau, the Minobu Line and Iida Line within the jurisdiction of the Shizuoka Railway Administration Bureau, the Oito Line within the jurisdiction of the Nagano Railway Administration Bureau, the Uno Line, Ako Line, and Fukuen Line within the jurisdiction of the Okayama Railway Administration Bureau, and the Ube Line and Onoda Line within the jurisdiction of the Hiroshima Railway Administration Bureau. In addition, some of the KuHa 68 type were used as control cars for the 70 series on provincial trunk lines such as the Shin'etsu Main Line (Niigata area) and Joetsu Line, the Shin'etsu Main Line (Nagano area), and the Chuo West Line.
章节.Converting KuMoHaYuni 44100 to KuMoHaYun:
In 1961, a flat-end non-through cab was added at the rear of KuMoHaYuni 44100, which was being used on the Oito Line, and its type and number were changed to the KuMoHaYuni 64 type (KuMoHaYuni 64000). At this time the coupler was also changed from a tight-lock coupler to an automatic coupler, so it did not enter commercial service, and was used in a way close to a private railway electric freight car, such as hauling freight cars or operating as a baggage EMU. Afterward, with the opening of electrification of the Ako Line in 1969 it was transferred to the Okayama Depot, and at the Suita Works the passenger compartment was made longitudinal seating and the rear cab was made through, returning to commercial service. In 1977 it was transferred to the Shizuoka Depot and used as a substitute tractor, but the following year, 1978, it was transferred again to the Inamatsushima Engine Depot and returned to commercial service. At the time of a general inspection at the Hamamatsu Works in 1981 (leaving on September 18) it was repainted from grape color to Yokosuka color, and as one of the last members of the old-type JNR EMUs it was active until its retirement in 1983.
Note that the designation KuMo (motor car with cab) Ha (ordinary car) Yu (mail car) Ni (baggage car) is one of the longest in JNR.
章节.Low-roof modification: In 1966 and 1967, and again in 1970 (two rounds), for the KuMoHa 51 type transferred to the Minobu Line to replace the 17 m-class KuMoHa 14 type, work was carried out at the Hamamatsu Works to lower the roof height at the pantograph mounting portion in order to secure insulation distance when passing through small-clearance tunnels; after the modification they were renumbered to the 800-number series. For incorporated cars from the 42 series that had a pantograph at the front, the pantograph was relocated to the rear at the time of the modification, and then the low-roof modification was carried out. The donor cars included both up (odd) and down (even) directions, but due to the policy of the Shizuoka Railway Administration Bureau, which had jurisdiction over the Minobu Line, the control motor cars on that line were unified to the down direction, so upon entering the line all up-direction cars were turned to face down. Therefore, all cars of this group were given even numbers. The renumbering is as follows.
章节.Toilet-installation modification:
On the KuHa 68 type used on the Iida Line, which operated long-distance services, installation of toilets began in 1961. The first to be modified was KuHa 68064, transferred in that year, and afterward it was carried out on the nine cars transferred from 1966 to 1967. At the time of the modification they kept their original numbers, but in May 1968 the ten cars that had been modified by then were renumbered to the 400-number series. Numbers were assigned odd and even according to the direction of the cab, but KuHa 68409 for some reason became an odd car—an odd-numbered car facing the down (even) direction. The donor cars were diverse, ranging from the original semi-streamlined KuHa 68 type to flat-end cars descended from the KuroHa 59 and KuHa 55. This modification was additionally carried out in 1972 and 1974, and in the end 16 cars became this number series.
1974 modification (3 cars)
KuHa 68416 ← KuHa 68026
KuHa 68418 ← KuHa 68066
KuHa 68420 ← KuHa 68094
章节.Cold- and snow-resistance modification:
For the 51 series transferred to the Senseki Line and the Niigata area, the following cold- and snow-resistance modifications were carried out.
Replacement of globe-type ventilators with push-in type ventilators (Senseki Line)
Relocation of the snow-covered horn to the run-number display window (Niigata area)
Fitting of snowplows (Niigata area)
章节.Chuo Line express EMUs:
The first place the 51 series EMUs were introduced was the Chuo Line express. From 1936 (Showa 11) to 1937, 26 MoHa 51 cars were newly built and all began use as lead cars toward Asakawa.
The present-day Chuo Line is constantly assigned new cars, but at the time new cars went preferentially to the Keihin Line, and the Chuo Line was mainly composed of old-type cars (many 17 m 30 series, early steel cars, and wooden trailer cars were assigned). For this reason, the 20 m, 3-door semi-cross-seat MoHa 51, combined with its half-compartment cab structure that gave a good view from the passenger compartment, won wide popularity from adults to children. However, the formations were uneven, mixing wooden cars and the 30 series, and especially when a wooden SaHa 25 was coupled behind a MoHa 51, the imbalance was such as could not be imagined from today's EMUs, which form formations of a single type.
章节.Yokosuka Line:
The final batch of the 51 series was the MoHaYuni 61 type, which appeared on the Yokosuka Line in 1943 (Showa 18) during the Pacific War. The plan to introduce the cars itself existed from around 1939 (Showa 14), but it was put off, and it ended up appearing in wartime. Therefore, it became a wartime design, with the seats made longitudinal and the work on various parts simplified. Also, due to a shortage of electrical components, all cars were completed as substitutes for control cars. After the war, 61002 and 61003 were transferred to the Iida Line, and the electrified 61001 to the Minobu Line.
After the war, from 1963 the 2-door 42, 32, and 52 series were converted to three doors and incorporated into the 51 series. The period during which the converted cars were used on the Yokosuka Line was short, and with the introduction of the 113 series, by 1965 the KuMoHa 51 200-number series had been transferred to the Minobu and Iida lines, the KuMoHa 50 type to the Iida Line, the KuHa 68 200- and 210-number series along with the 70 series to the Niigata area, and the SaHa 58 type to the Keihanshin local line and the Okayama area.
章节.Keihanshin local line:
The 51 series was introduced also for the Osaka Railway Bureau following the Chuo Line, and in 1937 (Showa 12) it was introduced to the ordinary trains (the Keihanshin local line) of the Tokaido Main Line and Sanyo Main Line, ahead of the opening of electrification between Kyoto Station and Suita Station. The introduction to the Chuo Line was only the MoHa 51 type, but to the Keihanshin local line all types except the MoHaYuni 61 were introduced, presenting a beauty of formation by a single type. The introduction of the 51 series continued until 1941 (Showa 16).
Initially it was assigned to the newly established Akashi Depot for the opening of Kyoto electrification, but some cars were also assigned to the Miyahara Depot and were sometimes put into express service.
During World War II, cars converted to longitudinal seating by wartime modifications appeared, but after the war, restoration to cross seating and the conversion of new 40-series longitudinal-seat cars to cross seating were carried out. In this process, all cars except 51073, which had been transferred to the Hanwa Line, and the mail-and-baggage combined car were gathered on the Keihanshin local line, and the 51 series, along with the 70 series introduced from 1951, became the mainstay type of the Keihanshin local line.
Even in the 1970s, a small number of KuMoHa 51 cars remained at both the Akashi and Takatsuki depots, and the KuHa 55 150-number series from the former KuroHa 69 were almost all assigned to Akashi (10 cars, excluding 55151, which was transferred to the Hanwa Line and written off in 1974), showing a remnant of the golden age of the 1950s alongside the 72 series. With the introduction of the 103 series, the operation of the 51 series ended in 1976.
章节.Joto Line and Katamachi Line: The 51 series was also newly assigned to the Yodogawa Depot and used to strengthen the transport capacity of the Joto Line (later the Osaka Loop Line) and the Katamachi Line. After World War II it was transferred to the Keihanshin local line.
章节.Hanwa Line:
To the Hanwa Line, the 3-door longitudinal-seat 40 series was transferred to replace the Hanwa-type EMUs, but from the 51 series as well the KuMoHa 51073, converted from the KuMoHa 42, was introduced. This car underwent modifications for three doors, single cab, and strengthened output, and was used on the Hanwa Line for a long time alongside the Hanwa-type EMUs, the MoHa 61 type that also received output-strengthening modifications at the same time, and the 70 series that appeared in 1955. In later years it was repainted orange.
KuMoHa 51073 was redeployed to the Minobu Line in 1970 due to the transfer in of the 72 series, and after undergoing the low-roof modification became KuMoHa 51830.
章节.Niigata and Nagano areas: In the Niigata and Nagano areas, the KuHa 68 type was used as control cars for the 70 series. The paint of cars for the Niigata area was changed to the so-called Niigata color of yellow and red. In 1978, both the Shin'etsu Main Line Nagano area and the Shinonoi Line, and the Niigata area lines (Shin'etsu Main Line, Joetsu Line, Hakushin Line, Uetsu Main Line) were replaced by the 115 series.
章节.Iida Line:
On the Iida Line, prewar-type JNR EMUs including the 51 series were transferred from the 1960s, and were used together with many types such as the 42 series and the Ryuden 52 series. Of the 51 series, the KuMoHa 51/54 types and KuHa 68 type were mainly used. The paint was unified to Yokosuka color in the latter half of the 1960s. KuMoHaYuni 64000 was transferred to the Iida Line in 1978 (as mentioned above), and was reunited with same-series cars (KuHaYuni 56011, 56012) from which it had been separated for decades.
Operation ended with the introduction of the 119 series in 1983. Note that after commercial operation on the Iida Line ended, the remaining cars were all written off the following year, 1984.
章节.Minobu Line:
The Minobu Line, together with the Iida Line, became one of the lines to which prewar-built JNR EMUs were redeployed, but to handle the small tunnels the cars used had undergone the low-roof modification. The paint was Yokosuka color.
Operation ended in 1981 with the introduction of the 115 series 2000-number series.
章节.Oito Line: On the Oito Line, 3-door longitudinal-seat 40-series transferred cars had been used since the 1960s, and from 1971 three KuMoHa 54 cars were transferred from the Senseki Line (see also the photo of KuMoHa 54101 in the upper row). The paint was changed to sky blue. Operation ended in 1981 with the replacement by the 115 series.
章节.Senseki Line: On the Senseki Line, 51 series cars were transferred in the 1960s, and the transferred cars underwent cold- and snow-resistance modifications. The paint became bush-warbler color, and they were operated as rapid-service trains. Operation ended in 1977 with the transfer in of the 72 series.
章节.Okayama area: In the Okayama area they were operated on the Uno Line, Ako Line, Sanyo Main Line, and others. Operation ended in 1976 with replacement by the 115 and 80 series.
章节.Fukuen Line: The 51 series redeployed to the electrified section between Fukuyama Station and Fuchu Station on the Fukuen Line was operated from 1971 with its paint changed to Aoi No. 20. In 1977 the 70 series EMUs were transferred in, and the operation of the 51 series on the Fukuen Line ended. In 1981 the 70 series too was replaced by the 105 series.
章节.Ube and Onoda lines: The 51 series redeployed to the Ube and Onoda lines, together with the old-performance EMUs on those lines, had a yellow warning color added to the lower front from 1974. With the introduction of newly built 105 series in 1981, they were replaced except for three KuMoHa 42 cars for the Motoyama Branch Line of the Onoda Line.
章节.Write-off:
The handy 51 series was active on each of the lines to which it was transferred, forming formations with prewar-type cars such as the 40 and 42 series. However, in the mid-1970s, about 40 years after its debut, its aging could no longer be concealed and replacement began. The cars for the Iida Line that lasted to the end were written off in 1984, and the type became extinct.

英文.全文:
The 51 series (51-kei densha) is a convenient collective designation for the 3-door semi-cross-seat old-type electric multiple units (EMUs) manufactured by the Ministry of Railways, the predecessor of Japanese National Railways, between 1936 (Showa 11) and 1943 (Showa 18). The 100 cars initially built comprised five types—MoHa 51, MoHa 54, MoHaYuni 61, KuHa 68, and KuroHa 69—but later, because many cars were converted and incorporated from the 40 and 42 series, numerous groups with differing body shapes and window arrangements came to exist within the same type. This article explains the 51 series chronologically from its debut to its demise, including conversions incorporated from other types.

== Debut ==
From the late Taisho era into the early Showa era, as electrification work within the Tokyo and Osaka urban areas steadily progressed, the operating sections of the government railway (provincial line) EMUs also expanded. As short-distance rolling stock, the 17 m steel 3-door longitudinal-seat 30 and 31 series appeared in the early Showa era, and in 1932 (Showa 7) the 40 series appeared as 3-door longitudinal-seat cars, becoming 20 m including the motor cars. Meanwhile, for medium- and long-distance use, in 1930 (Showa 5) the 2-door cross-seat 32 series appeared on the Yokosuka Line; the motor car MoHa 32 was 17 m, but the trailer cars appeared at 20 m. Subsequently, on the occasion of the opening of electrification of the Tokaido/Sanyo Line between Suita Station and Suma Station in 1934 (Showa 9), the 42 series appeared as 20 m, 2-door cross-seat cars including the motor cars. The 51 series appeared based on these types, as the first 3-door semi-cross-seat cars adopted by the government electric railways, so that comfortable service could be provided to passengers both at rush hour and during the daytime.
From 1936 it was introduced to the Chuo Line express in the Kanto region, and then in 1937 to the Keihanshin local line in the Kansai region. The final batch was the MoHaYuni 61 type, introduced to the Yokosuka Line in 1943.

== Basic types ==
The basic configuration of the body was a 3-door semi-cross-seat car with a window arrangement of d1D6D6D2, based on the semi-streamlined 40 series EMU that appeared in 1935; the windows on both sides of the doors in the longitudinal-seat section and at the car ends were 700 mm, and the remaining windows in the cross-seat section between the doors were 800 mm. As for the windows behind the driver's cab, cars built in 1936 that appeared with a half-compartment cab had 600 mm on the No. 1 side and 450 mm on the No. 2 side, while cars from 1937 onward with a full-compartment cab had 500 mm on both sides. The roof ventilators were in three rows, and except for the MoHaYuni 61 type, the cabs were of the through (gangway) type; except for cars assigned to the Chuo Line, gangway bellows were fitted between the cabs and between cars.
Each car was equipped with a PS11B pantograph, a 100 kW-class MT16 main motor, and an electro-pneumatic camshaft controller CS5; the gear ratio was 1:2.52 for cars introduced on the Chuo Line only, to match existing cars, while otherwise it was the same high-speed type 1:2.26 as the 32 and 42 series, and combined with the adoption of a motor that, though weak, had a relatively high rated speed at weak field, it was adapted to high-speed operation on the Keihanshin local line and the Yokosuka Line. As for bogies, the TR25 (DT12) common to the 40 and 42 series was used for motor cars, and the TR23 for trailer cars.
An outline of each type is as follows.

=== MoHa 51 ===
The MoHa 51 type was the core type of this series, a single-cab third-class control motor car of which 57 were built between 1936 and 1938. The appearance—a semi-streamlined body with a pantograph mounted at the rear of the body—was common to all years, but because they were built during a period when the manufacturing technology of prewar railway rolling stock was improving in both quality and quantity, the form differed by year of introduction. Cars that appeared in 1936 adopted a conventional headlight, a cloth-covered roof, and light-alloy passenger doors; cars that appeared in the first half of 1937 (built under the Showa 11 budget) adopted a bullet-shaped headlight and a steel-plate roof, and the running boards on the roof became two rows. Reacting to this, cars that appeared in the latter half of 1937 (built under the Showa 12 budget) adopted a raised (tensioned) roof, a design conscious of the then-fashionable streamline. Cars that appeared in 1938 adopted a semi-flush headlight on the same body as the latter-half-1937 cars, giving an even sleeker design, but as light alloys were diverted to military use with the expansion of the Second Sino-Japanese War, the passenger doors became wooden.
Cars introduced on the Chuo Line were set to the odd (up) direction regardless of their numbers, in order to be used entirely as lead cars facing Takao, and because the Tokyo government electric railways had no gangway bellows at the time, the connecting faces were hinged doors; thus, apart from the gear ratio, several points differed from cars introduced to the Keihanshin local line.
The manufacturing situation is as follows.

In addition, this type was later involved in a wide variety of conversions to other types and incorporations through conversion from other types. For the location of descriptions of cars that became this type (including the KuMoHa 51 type) through the latter, see the table on the right.

=== MoHa 54 ===
The MoHa 54 type was a single-cab third-class control motor car of which nine were built from 1937 to 1941; its main motor was changed to the newly designed high-output MT30, and accordingly the gear ratio was changed to 1:2.56. The 54001 and 54002 that appeared in 1937 had bodies no different from the cars of the MoHa 51 type that appeared in the first half of 1937, but making use of their high output, they incorporated in the middle a KuroHa 59 converted from SaRoHa 46 and a KuHa 58, and were put into express service alongside the 52 series and the semi-streamlined 43 series. The 54003 - 54005 that appeared in 1940 further refined the design of the 1938 cars, resulting in a beautiful body with no sill (window sill) or header, drawn inward, and no rivets, but the 54006 - 54009 that appeared the following year, affected by the material controls accompanying the strengthening of the wartime system, regressed to a design no different from the 1936 cars, with a wooden cloth-covered roof, wooden doors, and exposed window sills and headers.
The manufacturing situation is as follows.
1937

=== MoHaYuni 61 ===
The MoHaYuni 61 type was a third-class mail-and-baggage combined car, of which three (61001 - 61003) were built in 1943 by the Kisha Seizo branch to reinforce the mail and baggage cars of the Yokosuka Line.
Like the previously introduced MoHaYuni 44 type, the body was divided, from the front, into cab, baggage room, mail room, and third-class passenger room; the mail room had a double door 1,200 mm wide and the baggage room one 1,600 mm wide, with load capacities of 2 t of mail and 3 t of baggage. Like the MoHaYuni 44 type, being a combined car it had a non-through front; but it was semi-streamlined and its window arrangement was d1D (baggage) 2D (mail) 11D6D2, with a passenger door provided in the center, so its appearance was rather closer to the KuHaNi 67 type. Because the intensification of the Pacific War made the procurement of materials even more difficult, as noted above all cars entered service without electrical equipment, and only 61001 was electrified the following year. The rain gutters were also simplified with no vertical pipes, and drip edges were provided at the doors; the interior also appeared as a longitudinal-seat car with the seating halved.

=== KuHa 68 ===
The KuHa 68 type was a third-class control car of which 20 were built from 1937 to 1938, all facing the even (down) direction. The changes in form were the same as for the MoHa 51 type.
The manufacturing situation is as follows.

In addition, this type was later involved in a wide variety of cases: some were once converted to the KuHa 55 type and then returned to the KuHa 68 type after the war, and others were incorporated through conversion from other types. Descriptions of these cars are spread over various places, so see the table on the right for their locations.

=== KuroHa 69 ===
The KuroHa 69 type was a second- and third-class combined control car of which 11 were built in 1937, all facing the odd (up) direction. Its window arrangement was d1D6D222D2, and the second-class section had windows laid out to match the seating arrangement. As for form, apart from the KuroHa 69004 - 69007, which appeared with a raised roof like the cars of other types that appeared in the latter half of 1937, the cars were built in the same form as the cars that appeared in the first half of 1937.

== Wartime modifications ==
As the war became protracted, from the China Incident to the Pacific War, the railways too were incorporated into the wartime system. Above all, in order to transport in large numbers the laborers working in munitions factories, the following modifications were carried out while making do with scarce materials.

=== Converting the KuroHa 59 to the KuHa 68 ===
In November 1938, the second-class cars of the Keihanshin local line were abolished, and the KuroHa 59 type on local service were used with their second-class compartments downgraded as they were to third class; but from March 1941 to March 1942, 16 cars had a door added in the center of the body and were converted to the KuHa 68 type. Initially the plan was to target all the original KuroHa 59 type (59001 - 59021), but with the intensification of the war, from fiscal 1942 onward this was changed to the 3-door longitudinal-seat KuHa 55 type, producing gaps in the numbering.
68021 - 68035, 68037 ← 59001 - 59015, 59017
For details, see JNR 42 series EMU#Converting the KuroHa 59 to the KuHa 68.

=== Converting/incorporating the MoHa 40 and MoHa 41 into the MoHa 51 ===
At the time, the Osaka Railway Bureau drew up a plan to convert the 42 series to four doors and swap its bogies with those of the 40 series motor cars, put the four-door, low-speed 42 series onto the Joto and Nishinari lines, and instead put the 40 series motor cars fitted with the 42 series bogies onto the Keihanshin local line. Initially it was planned to convert all of the MoHa 40 and MoHa 41 cars belonging to the Osaka Railway Bureau into the MoHa 51 type, but with the worsening war situation, conversion from the MoHa 40 was carried out on only seven cars built in 1944 and 1945, and conversion from the MoHa 41 on only five cars built in 1943 and 1944. Of these, the cars converted from the MoHa 40 merely had the rear cab equipment and headlight removed, and the features as a lead car such as the crew door were left as they were (later, in the renewal repair, the crew-room door was filled in, seats installed, and a window provided). Because the seats were also removed at the same time, the character of the MoHa 51 type changed from a single-cab motor car with a 3-door body fitted with cross seats to a 3-door-body single-cab high-speed motor car.
The numbering was as follows, but because many cars were not modified, many gaps also occurred.

The reason renumbering occurred for cars converted from the MoHa 41 is that, due to a change in plan, the semi-streamlined 41053 - 41055 were to be given additional numbers to existing cars (51058 - 51060) (in practice not carried out).

=== Converting the MoHa 42 to the MoHa 51 ===
Of the MoHa 42 type, ten cars (42001 - 42010) were planned for a four-door, low-speed conversion (only five were modified before it was halted), but the remaining three (42011 - 42013) were to be converted to three doors, made single-cab, and converted to the MoHa 51 type. In 1944, 42012 was converted to 51073, but the rest ended up unmodified. For details, see JNR 42 series EMU#Modification of the MoHa 42.

=== Converting the MoHa 51 to the MoHa 41 with longitudinal seating and incorporating it ===
From 1943 to 1944, for the MoHa 51 type belonging to the Tokyo Railway Bureau (51001 - 51026, 26 cars), a conversion to longitudinal seating (removal of seats) from semi-cross seating was carried out at the Oi Engineering Works. At that time, because the MoHa 51 belonging to the Tokyo Railway Bureau had the same gear ratio as the 40 series, they were incorporated into the MoHa 41 type. The MoHa 51 and MoHa 54 types belonging to the Osaka Railway Bureau were also given a longitudinal-seating (seat-removal) conversion, but because their gear ratio differed from the 40 series, they kept their original numbers.
The old-new number comparison is as follows.

=== Converting the KuHa 68 and KuroHa 69 to the KuHa 55 with longitudinal seating and incorporating them ===
From 1943 to 1945, at the Suita Engineering Works, the KuHa 68 type (68001 - 68020, 20 cars, plus the 16 three-door-converted cars from the KuroHa 59 type, 68021 - 68035, 68037) and the KuroHa 69 type (69003 - 69011, 9 cars) were given longitudinal seating (seat removal) and incorporated into the KuHa 55 type. For the KuHa 68 type, only the longitudinal seating (removal) was carried out, but for the KuroHa 69 type, together with the third-class downgrading, modifications such as removing the partition with the second-class compartment were carried out at the same time. The course of the renumbering is as follows. Note that the KuroHa 69001 and 69002 were transferred to the Tokyo Railway Bureau and made spare cars for the Imperial family (in fact used on the Chuo/Sobu local line for the Imperial family's commute to the War College), so they remained as KuroHa.
The renumbering was done in the order of the KuHa 68 type prototype cars from the KuroHa 69 type, then the three-door-converted cars from the former KuroHa 59, given additional numbers of the KuHa 55 type; the reason 55106 - 55114 are gaps is that in the meantime these numbers were given to cars converted directly from the KuroHa 59 type to the KuHa 55 type. Also, the reason the KuroHa 69 numbers were swapped is that cars of the same form were given consecutive numbers and the 1937 latter-half raised-roof cars were moved together to the end.
As a result of these modifications, among the 3-door longitudinal-seat single-cab motor cars, the MoHa 41 type was organized as cars with a gear ratio of 1:2.52 and the MoHa 51 type as cars with a gear ratio of 1:2.26. Also, all control cars except 69001 and 69002, which remained as KuroHa, were incorporated into the KuHa 55 type.

== Restoration and incorporation modifications ==
Each type of the 51 series was converted to longitudinal seating by wartime modifications, and in the final stage of the war even more seats were removed to strengthen transport capacity, until eventually cars appeared with seats only in the door-engine portion. In the process of reconstruction after passing through the confused period immediately after the end of the war, the servicing and restoration of these devastated cars gradually proceeded (Renewal Repair I). Then, in the 1950s, in addition to restoration (servicing) modifications to semi-cross seating being carried out on the MoHa 51 type, including 40-series-converted cars, and on the KuHa 55 type, the former KuHa 68 type, cars of the MoHa 60 type and KuHa 55 type that had been built as 40 series and remained as they were during the war also appeared converted to semi-cross seating.

=== Restoring the MoHa 41 to the MoHa 51 ===
The 42 series that remained on the Keihanshin local line and express services after the war moved to the Yokosuka Line with the introduction of the 80 series in 1950, and instead 23 MoHa 41 cars (41056, 41058 - 41070, 41072 - 41080)—the former MoHa 51 cars of the Chuo Line that had escaped war damage—were transferred from the Tokyo Railway Bureau to the Keihanshin local line. For these MoHa 41 cars (the former MoHa 51), a restoration modification to semi-cross seating was carried out from 1951 to 1952, and to match performance with the other MoHa 51 cars the gear ratio was changed (1:2.52→1:2.26), and they reverted to their old numbers (51001, 51003 - 51015, 51017 - 51025).

=== Restoring the MoHa 51, MoHa 54, and KuHa 55 (former KuHa 68, former KuroHa 69) ===
At the same time as the above modifications, restoration modifications to 3-door semi-cross seating were carried out on the MoHa 51, MoHa 54, and KuHa 55 (former KuHa 68, former KuroHa 69) that had once been serviced as longitudinal-seat cars on the Keihanshin local line. This modification was also carried out on the MoHa 51 converted from the former MoHa 40 and MoHa 41, and on the former KuHa 68 converted from the former KuroHa 59.
In these processes, each type of 51 series origin that had been operated on the Joto and Nishinari lines and the Katamachi Line was transferred to the Keihanshin local line and restored to semi-cross seating.

=== Converting the MoHa 60 and KuHa 55 to semi-cross seating ===
Along with the above restoration modifications to semi-cross seating, semi-cross seating was also carried out on 21 MoHa 60 cars and 31 KuHa 55 cars that had been operated on the Keihanshin local line, out of the MoHa 60 and KuHa 55 types originally built as 3-door longitudinal-seat cars.
At this stage, because the cars that underwent the semi-cross-seating modification (restoration) were not renumbered, longitudinal-seat cars and semi-cross-seat cars came to be mixed within the MoHa 60 type and the KuHa 55 type.

=== Restoring the KuroHa 69 ===
Following the trend of the Allied-forces white-band cars, the second-class cars of the Keihanshin local line had been operated from November 1951 in a form in which the former white-band compartment was provisionally fitted out. In order to service this provisional KuroHa and provide quality service to second-class passengers, from 1952 to 1953, while recalling the 69001 and 69002 that had been transferred to the Tokyo Railway Bureau, a restoration modification to the KuroHa 69 type was carried out on the former KuroHa 69 cars 55097 - 55105 together with the servicing of 69001 and 69002. The work content went beyond the mere scope of restoration, being ambitious—rose-grey painted interiors, crimson moquette material, and the adoption of fluorescent lighting on some cars (69007, 69009)—bringing them close to the special second-class cars (Tokuro) that were the stars of the day, and those in charge prided themselves on it being the Tokuro of EMUs (though unlike the genuine Tokuro, the seats were not reclining). The renumbering was as follows, but because they were renumbered to the KuroHa 69 type while keeping the number order of the KuHa 55 type era, the raised-roof cars were moved together to the end, and only one car (69003) reverted to the same car number as before the war. In addition, because some had been serviced to all-compartment third-class cars before the 1953 revision of the vehicle type designation regulations, they were once incorporated into the KuHa 68 type at that time, and afterward the restoration servicing to the KuroHa 69 type was carried out again and they were renumbered. For 55102, renumbering to 68111 was planned, but because it was in the works, it became 69008 without going through renumbering to the KuHa 68 type.
Slightly off the point of this section, KuHa 55097 burned on March 1, 1952 within the Akashi Depot, but on May 28, 1953 at the Suita Works it was restored with a newly built body except for the front portion, and at the same time its second-class compartment was serviced and it became KuroHa 69003. At that time the body was manufactured entirely by welding, and the roof ventilator became a Garland-type single row, making it an odd car, but later, through Renewal Repair II, its appearance became almost the same as the other cars.

=== Converting the MoHaYuni 61 and KuHaNi 67 to the KuHaYuni 56 ===
To replace the company-type wooden third-class baggage-and-mail combined cars of the Iida Line, from 1951 to 1952 at the Toyokawa Branch Works, modifications were carried out on the KuHaNi 67 type to install a mail room (load 1 t) at the rear of the baggage room and to make the passenger compartment semi-cross seating and provide a toilet. At the same time, modifications to make the semi-cross seating and provide a toilet were also carried out on two of the MoHaYuni 61 type that remained unelectrified. The old-new number comparison is as follows.
In appearance there was almost no change from before the modification, and the characteristics of the donor car were retained as they were. The first car modified, 56001, had the width of the front passenger door narrowed during the modification, but this was brought in line with the other cars when Renewal Repair II was carried out. Note that this car was the only one among the KuHaNi 67-converted cars built in fiscal 1936, and it has window sills and headers above and below the windows. The only remaining 61001 had its interior serviced in 1951 and was made semi-cross seating.

== Changes accompanying the 1953 revision of the vehicle type designation regulations ==
In the 51 series, because the aforementioned semi-cross-seat-converted cars of the MoHa 60 and KuHa 55 types were incorporated into the two types MoHa 54 and KuHa 68, there was major movement in these types. As a result of renumbering according to the actual state of the semi-cross modification and restoration as shown below, in both the MoHa 54 and KuHa 68 types, the incorporated cars outnumbered the original cars.

=== Incorporating the MoHa 60 into the MoHa 54 ===
The 21 cars made cross-seat were incorporated into the MoHa 54 type (100-number series). The old-new number comparison is as follows.

=== Changing the KuHa 55 (former KuHa 68) to the KuHa 68 ===
In this group, 30 cars, excluding the 6 written off due to war damage, were incorporated into the KuHa 68 type (2nd generation). With this change, the former KuroHa 59 became 68001 - and the former KuHa 68 (original) became 68024 -, reversing the prewar numbering, and they were numbered divided into even and odd according to the direction of the cab. For reference, the history before the KuHa 55 conversion is also given again. For the incorporation of the former KuroHa 69 into the KuHa 68 type, see the section on restoring the KuroHa 69.

=== Incorporating the KuHa 55 into the KuHa 68 ===
From the original KuHa 55 type, 31 cars were incorporated into the KuHa 68 type. (See also JNR 40 series EMU#Semi-cross-seating of the MoHa 60 and KuHa 55 and the reorganization of cross-seat-converted cars.) This includes cars of every form—flat-end and semi-streamlined types, and no-sill/no-header cars. The old-new number comparison is as follows.
68060 - 68074 (even) ← 55013 - 55017, 55020, 55021, 55023 (flat-end)
68075, 68077 ← 55024, 55027 (flat-end)
68078 - 68092 (even) ← 55039, 55042, 55061, 55063, 55064, 55067, 55068, 55074 (semi-streamlined)
68093 - 68104, 68106 ← 55075 - 55080, 55087, 55082, 55089, 55084, 55091, 55086, 55092 (semi-streamlined)

=== Incorporating the MoHaYuni 61 into the MoHaYuni 44 100-number series ===
The only surviving car, 61001, was incorporated into the MoHaYuni 44 type, also a third-class baggage-and-mail combined car, and renumbered 44100. At this time the pantograph was relocated to the front. Around the same time it was transferred to the Kitamatsumoto Depot and came to be operated on the Oito Line.

== Renewal Repair II and other modifications ( - 1958) ==
In the 1950s, as the postwar confusion settled down somewhat, the measures taken to prevent train fires after the Sakuragicho accident were incorporated, and Renewal Repair (Renewal Repair II) came to be carried out again. The content differed depending on the works and the time, but the main work content is listed below.
Replacement of ventilators (Garland-type ventilator → globe-type ventilator)
To strengthen insulation, the raised steel-plate roof was made an ordinary wooden roof, and the rain-gutter position was unified to a lower position
Replacement of passenger doors with steel-plate pressed doors
Replacement of the wooden interior parts
Enlargement of the front run-number window (2 digits → 3 digits)
Filling in of the destination-display windows on the side fascia
Through this renewal repair, the variety of the original form, such as raised roofs and the number of ventilators, was almost lost, and the appearance became uniform. Not all of these work menu items were carried out on all cars; in the early period there were cars that kept their raised roofs while having globe-type ventilators fitted, and cars that remained with Garland-type ventilators. Also, because detailed specifications were changed according to the time of work, the variety of details became even richer.
In addition, the strengthened-illumination 250W headlight adopted to counter collision accidents with falling rocks on the Iida Line, having given good results, spread to all line sections using EMUs and was fitted to this series as well. At this time, the bullet-shaped and flush-mounted ones became the normal type, but some remained flush-mounted.
Other modifications are as follows.

=== Three-door conversion of 51073 (renewal repair) ===
51073, which was transferred to the Hanwa Line in 1950, was used for a while after its transfer in the very form of the MoHa 42 type. In the 1953 renewal repair it was made 3-door semi-cross seating, and the traces of the rear cab were smoothed out and a 550 mm-wide window was provided in the crew-door portion. As a result, the window arrangement also became d1D25D42D11. At the same time, the motor was also replaced with the MT30, the same as the MoHa 54 type, to strengthen the output. Before the renewal repair, 51073 was an odd car—a 2-door MoHa 51—but after the renewal repair, although it became 3-door, its motor output improved to the level of the MoHa 54 type, so in a different way from before it became an odd car among the MoHa 51 type.

=== Gear-ratio change of the MoHa 54 100-number series ===
Among the MoHa 54 type, the 100-number series incorporated from the MoHa 60 type, though made semi-cross seating, kept the gear ratio of the MoHa 60 type at 1:2.87. Since this would overload the main motor during high-speed operation, it was changed to 1:2.56, the same as the MoHa 54 prototype cars, at the time of the 1954 renewal repair, aligning it with the MoHa 51 and MoHa 70 types, which likewise had high-speed gear ratios.

=== Converting the KuHa 55 (KuroHa 59 converted from the former SaRoHa 46) to the KuHa 68 ===
The KuroHa 59 converted from the former SaRoHa 46, because its second-class compartment portion was wider than the KuroHa 59 prototype cars, was incorporated into express formations as noted above, so its downgrading conversion to KuHa 55 was late, in 1943. Of these, except for 59022, which was converted to four doors (via 55106, renumbered 85026 → 79056), 59023 - 59025 were converted to 55107 - 55109 without going through conversion to the KuHa 68 type. This group, together with the group converted directly from the KuroHa 59 type to the KuHa 55 type (55110 - 55114, of which 55114 was written off due to war damage), was excluded from the semi-cross-seating modification of the KuHa 55 type belonging to the Keihanshin local line, but to reinforce the semi-cross-seat cars of the Keihanshin local line, they underwent the semi-cross-seating modification from 1954 to 1955 and were incorporated into the KuHa 68 type. The renumbering is as follows.

Whereas the window arrangement of 68001 - 68023 converted from the former KuroHa 59 is d1D25D311D2, this group's is d1D231D42D2, which differs; also, the cab, while the former is a half-compartment cab, is a full-compartment cab here.

=== Converting 51078 to the Moya 4700 type ===
In 1958, 51078 was converted at the Toyokawa Branch Works into the overhead-wire test car Moya 4700. Because the body and bogies were newly built, only some of the electrical equipment used parts from the donor car. The following year, under the revision of the vehicle designation regulations, it was renumbered KuMoya 93000, and became famous for achieving, in 1960, the then-world record for narrow-gauge maximum speed of 175 km/h. Note that the donor car 51078 was a conversion from 41010, but there is a theory that, due to the wartime confusion, the actual car was swapped for 40001, the first-numbered MoHa 40.

== The 1959 revision of the vehicle designation regulations and commuter-oriented modifications ( - 1963) ==
Under this revision, motor cars with a cab became control motor cars (symbol: Kumo), so the MoHa 51 type was renamed KuMoHa 51 and the MoHa 54 type KuMoHa 54. Also, whereas previously types were expressed by numbers alone, from this revision the type symbol and the number were combined to form the type (e.g., type 69 → type KuroHa 69).
Also, from this period, modifications were carried out to cope with the intensifying commuter transport.

=== Downgrading conversion of the KuroHa 69 ===
The KuroHa 69 type, which after the second-class restoration had been active as the star of the Keihanshin local line, saw its raison d'etre decline after the coupling of SaRo 85 cars to rapid services began in 1961. In October 1962 the coupling of KuroHa cars on the Keihanshin local line was abolished on the grounds of easing congestion, so over the following year the partitions of the first-class and second-class compartments (changed to a two-class system from 1960) were removed, longitudinal seating was adopted, and a downgrading conversion to the KuHa 55 type (KuHa 55151 - 55171 (odd numbers only)) was carried out. The work was done at the Suita Works for 55104(55151) and at the Hatsukaichi Works for the rest. The old-new number comparison is as follows.

Also, because the renumbering of KuroHa 69004 - 69007 was later, as a result, apart from KuHa 55151, they are in the number order at the time the KuroHa 69 type was newly built.

=== Door-addition modification of the Yokosuka Line 2-door cars ===
From 1963 to 1964, for the 2-door KuMoHa 43 and KuMoHa 53 (42 series), KuHa 47 (32 series), and SaHa 48 (52 series) remaining on the Yokosuka Line, in order to cope with the intensified commuter transport, to align the boarding positions when coupled with the 3-door 70 series, and to avoid disturbing orderly queuing, work was carried out at the Ofuna Works to add a passenger door in the center of the body and convert them to three doors. After the modification, the KuMoHa 43 type was changed to the KuMoHa 51 type (200-number series) and the KuHa 47 type to the KuHa 68 type (200-number series, 210-number series), while the KuMoHa 53 type and SaHa 48 type were given the new types KuMoHa 50 and SaHa 58 respectively. Of these, only KuHa 47002 was a car used on the Iida Line, but both the time of modification and the time of transfer out to the Niigata area were almost the same as for the other cars belonging to the Yokosuka Line. The renumbering situation is as follows.
Of these, the KuHa 68 200-number series are conversions from the KuHa 47 prototype cars, and the KuHa 68 210-number series are conversions from SaHa 48-converted cars. The reason the SaHa 58 has finely divided number series relative to its count is that the donor cars each differ (0-number series ← SaHa 48 of the narrow-window Ryuden formation, 10-number series ← SaHa 48 of the semi-streamlined 43 series formation, 20-number series ← SaHa 48 of the wide-window Ryuden formation, 50-number series ← SaHa 48 converted from the former SaRoHa 66 of the wide-window Ryuden formation); SaHa 58050 appeared at the time of renewal repair retaining its raised roof (in later years its rain gutters were modified to the same height as the other cars, but whereas the others were wooden, these were steel). Also, with the appearance of the KuMoHa 50 type, it would not have been strange to incorporate the KuMoHa 51073, a 42-series-converted output-strengthened car, into the KuMoHa 50, and there apparently was a plan to renumber it KuMoHa 50051, but in the end, without renumbering, it was converted to KuMoHa 51830. The side window arrangement of this group is made front-rear asymmetric with an independent door-pocket window supported by H rubber behind the door newly provided in the center, differing from KuMoHa 51073 (for example, the KuMoHa 50 type and KuMoHa 51 200-number series are d1D24D142D2).
Note that KuMoHa 50006 was involved in the Tsurumi accident that occurred on November 9, 1963 immediately after leaving the works; the body was wrecked beyond recognition and the car was written off.

=== Increase in renewal-repair specifications ===
From around this time, examples came to be seen of extensive use of H rubber on the cab windows and door-pocket windows to prevent corrosion from rainwater ingress; among these, in cars worked at the Suita Works, when the cab windows were H-rubbered, a hemispherical ventilator was fitted beside the gangway door, and together with the H-rubbered and miniaturized cab windows this formed a distinctive front. Also, of the cars fitted with hemispherical ventilators, many filled in the louvers above the cab windows, but some cars remained as they were.

== Transfer to the provinces (1960 - ) ==
The 51 series, which had been used as the mainstay of the Keihanshin local line, from the 1960s gradually came to be transferred to provincial lines, with the transfer of 72 series to the Keihanshin local line and the new-build assignment of 103 series accompanying the strengthening of transport capacity and the opening of newly electrified sections. Also, cars assigned to the Yokosuka Line and Hanwa Line were transferred to provincial lines as each line section's cars were replaced. Upon transfer to provincial lines, modifications such as lowering the roof and installing toilets according to the circumstances of the line section were carried out; in addition, to cope with gradients and short inter-station distances, mainly on cars assigned to the Shizuoka Railway Administration Bureau, the gears were changed to the same low-speed type as the 40 series.
The lines to which they were redeployed were mostly lines acquired from private railways during the war—the Senseki Line within the jurisdiction of the Sendai Railway Administration Bureau, the Minobu Line and Iida Line within the jurisdiction of the Shizuoka Railway Administration Bureau, the Oito Line within the jurisdiction of the Nagano Railway Administration Bureau, the Uno Line, Ako Line, and Fukuen Line within the jurisdiction of the Okayama Railway Administration Bureau, and the Ube Line and Onoda Line within the jurisdiction of the Hiroshima Railway Administration Bureau. In addition, some of the KuHa 68 type were used as control cars for the 70 series on provincial trunk lines such as the Shin'etsu Main Line (Niigata area) and Joetsu Line, the Shin'etsu Main Line (Nagano area), and the Chuo West Line.

=== Converting KuMoHaYuni 44100 to KuMoHaYuni 64000 ===
In 1961, a flat-end non-through cab was added at the rear of KuMoHaYuni 44100, which was being used on the Oito Line, and its type and number were changed to the KuMoHaYuni 64 type (KuMoHaYuni 64000). At this time the coupler was also changed from a tight-lock coupler to an automatic coupler, so it did not enter commercial service, and was used in a way close to a private railway electric freight car, such as hauling freight cars or operating as a baggage EMU. Afterward, with the opening of electrification of the Ako Line in 1969 it was transferred to the Okayama Depot, and at the Suita Works the passenger compartment was made longitudinal seating and the rear cab was made through, returning to commercial service. In 1977 it was transferred to the Shizuoka Depot and used as a substitute tractor, but the following year, 1978, it was transferred again to the Inamatsushima Engine Depot and returned to commercial service. At the time of a general inspection at the Hamamatsu Works in 1981 (leaving on September 18) it was repainted from grape color to Yokosuka color, and as one of the last members of the old-type JNR EMUs it was active until its retirement in 1983.
Note that the designation KuMo (motor car with cab) Ha (ordinary car) Yu (mail car) Ni (baggage car) is one of the longest in JNR.

=== Low-roof modification ===
In 1966 and 1967, and again in 1970 (two rounds), for the KuMoHa 51 type transferred to the Minobu Line to replace the 17 m-class KuMoHa 14 type, work was carried out at the Hamamatsu Works to lower the roof height at the pantograph mounting portion in order to secure insulation distance when passing through small-clearance tunnels; after the modification they were renumbered to the 800-number series. For incorporated cars from the 42 series that had a pantograph at the front, the pantograph was relocated to the rear at the time of the modification, and then the low-roof modification was carried out. The donor cars included both up (odd) and down (even) directions, but due to the policy of the Shizuoka Railway Administration Bureau, which had jurisdiction over the Minobu Line, the control motor cars on that line were unified to the down direction, so upon entering the line all up-direction cars were turned to face down. Therefore, all cars of this group were given even numbers. The renumbering is as follows.

=== Toilet-installation modification ===
On the KuHa 68 type used on the Iida Line, which operated long-distance services, installation of toilets began in 1961. The first to be modified was KuHa 68064, transferred in that year, and afterward it was carried out on the nine cars transferred from 1966 to 1967. At the time of the modification they kept their original numbers, but in May 1968 the ten cars that had been modified by then were renumbered to the 400-number series. Numbers were assigned odd and even according to the direction of the cab, but KuHa 68409 for some reason became an odd car—an odd-numbered car facing the down (even) direction. The donor cars were diverse, ranging from the original semi-streamlined KuHa 68 type to flat-end cars descended from the KuroHa 59 and KuHa 55. This modification was additionally carried out in 1972 and 1974, and in the end 16 cars became this number series.

== Operation ==

=== Kanto region ===

==== Chuo Line express EMUs ====
The first place the 51 series EMUs were introduced was the Chuo Line express. From 1936 (Showa 11) to 1937, 26 MoHa 51 cars were newly built and all began use as lead cars toward Asakawa.
The present-day Chuo Line is constantly assigned new cars, but at the time new cars went preferentially to the Keihin Line, and the Chuo Line was mainly composed of old-type cars (many 17 m 30 series, early steel cars, and wooden trailer cars were assigned). For this reason, the 20 m, 3-door semi-cross-seat MoHa 51, combined with its half-compartment cab structure that gave a good view from the passenger compartment, won wide popularity from adults to children. However, the formations were uneven, mixing wooden cars and the 30 series, and especially when a wooden SaHa 25 was coupled behind a MoHa 51, the imbalance was such as could not be imagined from today's EMUs, which form formations of a single type.

==== Yokosuka Line ====
The final batch of the 51 series was the MoHaYuni 61 type, which appeared on the Yokosuka Line in 1943 (Showa 18) during the Pacific War. The plan to introduce the cars itself existed from around 1939 (Showa 14), but it was put off, and it ended up appearing in wartime. Therefore, it became a wartime design, with the seats made longitudinal and the work on various parts simplified. Also, due to a shortage of electrical components, all cars were completed as substitutes for control cars. After the war, 61002 and 61003 were transferred to the Iida Line, and the electrified 61001 to the Minobu Line.
After the war, from 1963 the 2-door 42, 32, and 52 series were converted to three doors and incorporated into the 51 series. The period during which the converted cars were used on the Yokosuka Line was short, and with the introduction of the 113 series, by 1965 the KuMoHa 51 200-number series had been transferred to the Minobu and Iida lines, the KuMoHa 50 type to the Iida Line, the KuHa 68 200- and 210-number series along with the 70 series to the Niigata area, and the SaHa 58 type to the Keihanshin local line and the Okayama area.

=== Kansai region ===

==== Keihanshin local line ====
The 51 series was introduced also for the Osaka Railway Bureau following the Chuo Line, and in 1937 (Showa 12) it was introduced to the ordinary trains (the Keihanshin local line) of the Tokaido Main Line and Sanyo Main Line, ahead of the opening of electrification between Kyoto Station and Suita Station. The introduction to the Chuo Line was only the MoHa 51 type, but to the Keihanshin local line all types except the MoHaYuni 61 were introduced, presenting a beauty of formation by a single type. The introduction of the 51 series continued until 1941 (Showa 16).
Initially it was assigned to the newly established Akashi Depot for the opening of Kyoto electrification, but some cars were also assigned to the Miyahara Depot and were sometimes put into express service.
During World War II, cars converted to longitudinal seating by wartime modifications appeared, but after the war, restoration to cross seating and the conversion of new 40-series longitudinal-seat cars to cross seating were carried out. In this process, all cars except 51073, which had been transferred to the Hanwa Line, and the mail-and-baggage combined car were gathered on the Keihanshin local line, and the 51 series, along with the 70 series introduced from 1951, became the mainstay type of the Keihanshin local line.
Even in the 1970s, a small number of KuMoHa 51 cars remained at both the Akashi and Takatsuki depots, and the KuHa 55 150-number series from the former KuroHa 69 were almost all assigned to Akashi (10 cars, excluding 55151, which was transferred to the Hanwa Line and written off in 1974), showing a remnant of the golden age of the 1950s alongside the 72 series. With the introduction of the 103 series, the operation of the 51 series ended in 1976.

==== Joto Line and Katamachi Line ====
The 51 series was also newly assigned to the Yodogawa Depot and used to strengthen the transport capacity of the Joto Line (later the Osaka Loop Line) and the Katamachi Line. After World War II it was transferred to the Keihanshin local line.

==== Hanwa Line ====
To the Hanwa Line, the 3-door longitudinal-seat 40 series was transferred to replace the Hanwa-type EMUs, but from the 51 series as well the KuMoHa 51073, converted from the KuMoHa 42, was introduced. This car underwent modifications for three doors, single cab, and strengthened output, and was used on the Hanwa Line for a long time alongside the Hanwa-type EMUs, the MoHa 61 type that also received output-strengthening modifications at the same time, and the 70 series that appeared in 1955. In later years it was repainted orange.
KuMoHa 51073 was redeployed to the Minobu Line in 1970 due to the transfer in of the 72 series, and after undergoing the low-roof modification became KuMoHa 51830.

=== Chubu, Shin'etsu, and Tohoku regions ===

==== Niigata and Nagano areas ====
In the Niigata and Nagano areas, the KuHa 68 type was used as control cars for the 70 series. The paint of cars for the Niigata area was changed to the so-called Niigata color of yellow and red. In 1978, both the Shin'etsu Main Line Nagano area and the Shinonoi Line, and the Niigata area lines (Shin'etsu Main Line, Joetsu Line, Hakushin Line, Uetsu Main Line) were replaced by the 115 series.

==== Iida Line ====
On the Iida Line, prewar-type JNR EMUs including the 51 series were transferred from the 1960s, and were used together with many types such as the 42 series and the Ryuden 52 series. Of the 51 series, the KuMoHa 51/54 types and KuHa 68 type were mainly used. The paint was unified to Yokosuka color in the latter half of the 1960s. KuMoHaYuni 64000 was transferred to the Iida Line in 1978 (as mentioned above), and was reunited with same-series cars (KuHaYuni 56011, 56012) from which it had been separated for decades.
Operation ended with the introduction of the 119 series in 1983. Note that after commercial operation on the Iida Line ended, the remaining cars were all written off the following year, 1984.

==== Minobu Line ====
The Minobu Line, together with the Iida Line, became one of the lines to which prewar-built JNR EMUs were redeployed, but to handle the small tunnels the cars used had undergone the low-roof modification. The paint was Yokosuka color.
Operation ended in 1981 with the introduction of the 115 series 2000-number series.

==== Oito Line ====
On the Oito Line, 3-door longitudinal-seat 40-series transferred cars had been used since the 1960s, and from 1971 three KuMoHa 54 cars were transferred from the Senseki Line (see also the photo of KuMoHa 54101 in the upper row). The paint was changed to sky blue. Operation ended in 1981 with the replacement by the 115 series.

==== Senseki Line ====
On the Senseki Line, 51 series cars were transferred in the 1960s, and the transferred cars underwent cold- and snow-resistance modifications. The paint became bush-warbler color, and they were operated as rapid-service trains. Operation ended in 1977 with the transfer in of the 72 series.

=== Chugoku region ===

==== Okayama area ====
In the Okayama area they were operated on the Uno Line, Ako Line, Sanyo Main Line, and others. Operation ended in 1976 with replacement by the 115 and 80 series.

==== Fukuen Line ====
The 51 series redeployed to the electrified section between Fukuyama Station and Fuchu Station on the Fukuen Line was operated from 1971 with its paint changed to Aoi No. 20. In 1977 the 70 series EMUs were transferred in, and the operation of the 51 series on the Fukuen Line ended. In 1981 the 70 series too was replaced by the 105 series.

==== Ube and Onoda lines ====
The 51 series redeployed to the Ube and Onoda lines, together with the old-performance EMUs on those lines, had a yellow warning color added to the lower front from 1974. With the introduction of newly built 105 series in 1981, they were replaced except for three KuMoHa 42 cars for the Motoyama Branch Line of the Onoda Line.

== Write-off ==
The handy 51 series was active on each of the lines to which it was transferred, forming formations with prewar-type cars such as the 40 and 42 series. However, in the mid-1970s, about 40 years after its debut, its aging could no longer be concealed and replacement began. The cars for the Iida Line that lasted to the end were written off in 1984, and the type became extinct.
